newsitem.title: USA: IMF to help crack down on money launderers.
newsitem.headline: IMF to help crack down on money launderers.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will help countries crack down on money laundering, which it said could undermine their financial stability, the Fund's managing director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday.
Camdessus told a news conference that the IMF and the World Bank, together with regional development banks, stood ready to provide countries with funding and technical advice to combat the crime.
"We are going to make life a little more difficult for launderers," he said at the end of the annual IMF/World Bank meeting of the world's financial authorities.
Money laundering is the mainstay of the international drug trade, which seeks to get vast sums of illegal profits back into circulation through the financial system.
Drug traffickers often target off-shore financial centres as safe places to stash their funds.
Camdessus endorsed studies conducted by IMF economists who concluded that money laundering could jeopardise countries' financial systems and undermine their economic stability.

In the course of reviewing the health of countries' banking sectors, the IMF will advise governments on the strength of their regulations and enforcement procedures to close the gaps that allow criminals to launder money.
Regarding banking secrecy laws -- on which many off-shore banking industries are founded -- Camdessus said the IMF had not yet discussed them with member countries who have such rules on their books.
Once it has studied the impact of such laws on money laundering, the IMF could make a recommendation to countries on whether they should scrap those rules.
